title: Coin Change Problem
description: Understand how Greedy Algorithms solve the Coin Change Problem by selecting the largest denominations first.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Coin Change Problem is one of the most common examples used to demonstrate greedy problem solving.

The objective is to determine the minimum number of coins needed to represent a target amount.

Greedy strategies attempt to solve this efficiently by always selecting the largest possible coin denomination first.

sections.title: Understanding the Problem
sections.content:
Suppose a system contains several coin denominations such as 1, 5, 10, and 25.

The algorithm must repeatedly choose coins until the target amount is reached.

The goal is to minimize the total number of coins used.

sections.title: The Greedy Solution
sections.content:
The greedy strategy selects the largest denomination that does not exceed the remaining amount.

After choosing a coin, the remaining value is reduced and the process repeats.

For many currency systems, this approach successfully produces an optimal solution quickly and efficiently.

sections.title: When Greedy Fails
sections.content:
Although greedy solutions work well for many currency systems, they do not always guarantee optimal results.

Certain coin combinations may produce better solutions that the greedy approach cannot discover because it focuses only on immediate choices.

This limitation demonstrates why some problems require Dynamic Programming instead.

sections.title: Cashier Analogy
sections.content:
Imagine a cashier returning change to a customer.

To minimize the number of coins or bills used, the cashier usually gives the largest denominations first.

This mirrors the greedy strategy used in the Coin Change Problem.

sections.title: Greedy Optimization in Real Applications
sections.content:
Greedy optimization strategies are used in financial systems, vending machines, and automated transaction systems.

These systems prioritize fast decision-making because efficiency is often more important than exploring every possible solution.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: The Coin Change Problem demonstrates how Greedy Algorithms make locally optimal decisions by repeatedly selecting the largest denomination available. While efficient, greedy solutions may not always produce globally optimal answers.
